simple: combining many numbers into one, such as a sum or a maximum, with many threads at once.
analogy: every row of helpers adds up its own pile, then the row leaders add their totals.
precise: an associative combine applied as a tree: within a wave (shuffles), within a workgroup (LDS) and across workgroups (a second pass or atomics); with floating point the tree's order changes the rounding.
source: D1 of F7-15 (AMD, rocPRIM and hipCUB documentation) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); tree-order runs R of F7-15

simple: for each position, the total of everything before it (or up to and including it).
analogy: each helper writes down the running count of jars so far in the line.
precise: inclusive or exclusive prefix combine; on GPUs computed per wave with shuffles, per workgroup through LDS and across workgroups with a reduce-then-scan or a decoupled look-back pass.
source: D1 of F7-15 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's library of fast building blocks such as scan, reduce and sort, written for AMD GPUs.
analogy: the sister hall's book of proven recipes for counting and sorting.
precise: ROCm's C++ header library of device-wide, block-wide and warp-wide parallel primitives; not installed in this build, so its API names are unverified here.
source: D1 of F7-15 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a version of NVIDIA's CUB library interface that works on AMD GPUs by calling rocPRIM.
analogy: the same recipe book cover, with the sister hall's recipes inside.
precise: a thin HIP library exposing CUB's interface; on AMD it forwards to rocPRIM, on NVIDIA to CUB. Not installed in this build; CUB 2.0.1 was compiled instead.
source: D1 of F7-15 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); CUB headers read (H1 of F7-15)

simple: calling a library function once to ask how much scratch memory it needs, then again to do the work.
analogy: asking the stores how many trays the job needs before starting it.
precise: the CUB/hipCUB convention: with a null temporary-storage pointer the call only writes the required byte count; the caller allocates it and calls again with the same arguments.
source: CUB 2.0.1 headers (H1 of F7-15), compiled in this build

simple: a way for each block of a scan to find the total of all blocks before it without a second pass over the data.
analogy: each table looks at the tables before it, taking a finished running total when one is posted, otherwise a partial count, until it can add everything up.
precise: single-pass scan in which each tile publishes an aggregate and then an inclusive prefix with status flags; a tile reads predecessors' entries backwards until it meets an inclusive prefix (Merrill and Garland).
source: D2 of F7-15 (Merrill and Garland, single-pass parallel prefix scan) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); simulation in lookback.cpp

simple: getting exactly the same bits every time the same program runs on the same input.
analogy: weighing the same pile twice and reading the same weight both times.
precise: bitwise-identical results across runs; broken by atomics with nondeterministic order and, across GPUs, by different reduction trees (for example wave32 versus wave64), because floating-point addition is not associative.
source: tree_order run of F7-15

simple: the general matrix multiply: C becomes alpha times A times B plus beta times C.
analogy: the hall's biggest standard order, which every bench is measured on.
precise: general matrix-matrix multiplication, C = αAB + βC, with 2MNK floating-point operations; the BLAS level-3 routine (SGEMM single, HGEMM half precision).
source: D1 of F7-16 (BLAS reference) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the small fast memory on an AMD compute unit that the threads of one workgroup share.
analogy: the shared table in the middle of each work area.
precise: AMD's on-chip per-CU scratchpad addressed with ds_* instructions, at most 64 KiB per workgroup in this build's compiler ("local memory (65540) exceeds limit (65536)"); the counterpart of CUDA shared memory.
source: lds_limit run of F7-16; D2 of F7-16 (AMD CDNA ISA guide) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a piece of the matrices that a whole workgroup copies into shared memory and reuses many times.
analogy: bringing one tray of ingredients to the shared table so the whole team can use it.
precise: a BM×BK slice of A and BK×BN slice of B staged in LDS per k-step, so each global element is loaded once per tile instead of once per use.
source: F7-16 runs (resources, inner_loop)

simple: each thread computes a small block of results and keeps them in its own registers.
analogy: each helper works on a small 4-by-4 patch on their own board.
precise: each work-item accumulates a TM×TN sub-tile of C in VGPRs and reuses each loaded A and B value TN and TM times, raising arithmetic intensity at the cost of registers.
source: inner_loop run of F7-16 (vgpr 76 for 4x4)

simple: how much computing a program does for each byte it moves.
analogy: how many dishes you cook for each trip to the pantry.
precise: floating-point operations per byte of memory traffic at a given level of the memory hierarchy; compared with the machine's balance point in the roofline model.
source: tile_math run of F7-16; D3 of F7-16 (Williams, Waterman and Patterson, roofline) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: overwriting shared data while another part of the team still needs the old version.
analogy: clearing the table for the next tray while someone is still reading from it.
precise: in a tiled loop, a wave that starts loading tile k+1 into LDS before all waves finished reading tile k; prevented by a barrier between the last read and the next write (or by double buffering).
source: tiled_replay and kai_isa runs of F7-16

simple: special hardware in a GPU that multiplies small matrix blocks in one instruction.
analogy: a machine that does a whole tray of multiplications in one go.
precise: per-CU matrix units used by MFMA on CDNA (and WMMA on RDNA3 for a different shape); NVIDIA's counterpart is the tensor core.
source: targets run of F7-17; D1 of F7-17 (AMD CDNA ISA guide) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's matrix fused multiply-add instructions that use the matrix cores.
analogy: the order slip for the tray machine.
precise: v_mfma_* instructions on CDNA (gfx908, gfx90a, gfx94x), for example v_mfma_f32_32x32x8f16, multiplying wave-distributed fragments and accumulating into VGPRs or AGPRs; compiling them for gfx1030/gfx1100 fails with "needs target feature mai-insts".
source: targets and isa_gemm runs of F7-17

simple: the part of a small matrix each lane holds when a wave does a matrix instruction together.
analogy: which ingredients each helper hands to the tray machine.
precise: the mapping from matrix elements to (lane, register) for each MFMA/WMMA operand and result; shape- and architecture-specific, defined in the ISA guide (unverified in this build).
source: D1 of F7-17 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: extra registers on some AMD GPUs that hold matrix results.
analogy: a separate rack next to the tray machine for finished trays.
precise: accumulation VGPRs on CDNA; on gfx908 MFMA results live only there (.agpr_count 16 in this build), on gfx90a they share the unified register file with ordinary VGPRs (accum_offset).
source: isa_gemm run of F7-17

simple: an AMD library that lets C++ code use matrix cores with a simple fragment interface.
analogy: a simple form for ordering from the tray machine without knowing how it works.
precise: ROCm's header library modelled on CUDA's nvcuda::wmma (load_matrix_sync, mma_sync, store_matrix_sync); not installed in this build, so its names are unverified here.
source: D2 of F7-17 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); CUDA mma.h compiled (cuda_wmma run)

simple: doing multiplications with small, fast numbers but adding the results with bigger, more exact numbers.
analogy: measuring each scoop roughly but keeping the total on a precise scale.
precise: FP16 or BF16 inputs with FP32 accumulation, as in v_mfma_f32_32x32x8f16; error grows with K more slowly than with FP16 accumulation.
source: fp16_error run of F7-17

simple: an AMD library that builds fast GPU kernels from templates with many settings.
analogy: a kit of interchangeable tray and row parts, assembled per order.
precise: AMD's C++ template library for GEMM, convolution and attention kernels composed from tile operations; instances are template specialisations with tuning parameters and an argument-support check. Not installed in this build.
source: D1 of F7-18 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one ready-to-use kernel made by filling in all the settings of a template.
analogy: one fully assembled bench from the kit.
precise: a fully specialised kernel template (tile sizes, thread tile, padding, data types) compiled into the binary; libraries ship many and pick one per problem.
source: instances run of F7-18

simple: a setting that changes speed but should not change the answer.
analogy: how big the trays are and how many helpers per table.
precise: a compile-time or run-time choice such as BM, BN, BK, TM, TN, block size or padding, chosen by measurement per GPU and problem shape.
source: F7-18 runs

simple: a test a kernel runs before starting to make sure it can handle the given sizes.
analogy: checking that the order fits the tray size before accepting it.
precise: a host function (IsSupportedArgument in CK) that rejects problem shapes an instance cannot compute correctly, such as K not a multiple of BK without padding; skipping it gives silent wrong results.
source: nightly run of F7-18; D1 of F7-18 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the nesting of work pieces: the whole matrix, block tiles, wave tiles and thread tiles.
analogy: the order, each table's share, each row's share and each helper's patch.
precise: the decomposition of a GEMM into workgroup tiles (LDS), wave tiles and per-lane register tiles (or matrix-instruction fragments), each sized from the one above.
source: F7-18 static_asserts (instances run)

simple: a version of a kernel that handles sizes that do not fit the tiles evenly.
analogy: a bench that can take an order smaller than a full tray.
precise: an instance variant that bounds-checks or pads partial tiles (GemmSpecialization in CK); without it, the support check must reject sizes that are not tile multiples.
source: nightly run of F7-18

simple: a standard list of basic matrix and vector operations that many libraries implement.
analogy: the standard menu every hall knows by name.
precise: Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms: level 1 (vector), 2 (matrix-vector) and 3 (matrix-matrix, GEMM), with the column-major and leading-dimension conventions of the reference implementation.
source: D1 of F7-19 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's BLAS library for its GPUs.
analogy: the sister hall's master team for matrix orders.
precise: ROCm's BLAS implementation (rocblas_sgemm and others, with a handle and column-major arguments); not installed in this build, so its API is unverified here.
source: D2 of F7-19 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); cuBLAS 12.0.2 compiled instead

simple: AMD's flexible GEMM library with many options such as data types and fused extras.
analogy: the master team's special-orders desk.
precise: ROCm's lightweight GEMM library modelled on cuBLASLt (matmul descriptors, layouts, preferences and heuristics); not installed in this build.
source: D2 of F7-19 — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); cuBLASLt headers read

simple: the distance in memory from one column (or row) of a matrix to the next.
analogy: how far apart the shelves are, which can be wider than what is on them.
precise: in column-major BLAS, element (i, j) is at A[i + j·lda] with lda ≥ rows; it lets a routine work on a sub-matrix of a bigger array.
source: colmajor run of F7-19

simple: how fast your kernel is compared with the vendor's own library, as a percentage.
analogy: your bench's time compared with the master team's on the same order.
precise: time_reference / time_yours × 100 (equal to throughput ratio) for the same problem, measured with the same protocol and with both sides warmed up; meaningless without versions and hardware.
source: harness and cold_ref runs of F7-19

simple: running something a few times before timing it, so start-up costs are not counted.
analogy: letting the oven heat before timing a bake.
precise: untimed iterations before measurement that absorb one-time costs (code loading, allocation, caches, clocks); must be applied equally to the kernel and the reference.
source: cold_ref and cold_ref_fixed runs of F7-19

simple: one program that is not only correct but also reasonably fast on different GPUs.
analogy: one set of recipe cards that works well in both halls.
precise: the property that a single source reaches a stated fraction of each platform's achievable performance (here: the vendor library on each GPU), measured per kernel; correctness portability is the weaker property.
source: C1 of F7-20 (Systems Curriculum, milestone E9; a map, not a source, AH-4)

simple: the compiler reads a HIP file several times: once for the CPU part and once for each GPU target.
analogy: the same card read once by the hall manager and once by each kind of row.
precise: in single-source GPU compilation the host code is compiled once and device code once per offload target, each with its own predefined macros; in this build the hipcc host pass defined __AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE 64 but no __gfx*__ macro.
source: macros run of F7-20

simple: one program file that carries machine code for several GPUs.
analogy: one recipe folder with a card for each kind of hall.
precise: an executable whose GPU section bundles one code object per offload target (here hipv4-amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx90a and --gfx1100); the runtime loads the one matching the GPU.
source: fatbin run of F7-20; D2 of F7-20 (LLVM offload bundler documentation) — Title only — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number with one bit per lane of a wave, saying which lanes answered yes.
analogy: a row of 64 hands, each up or down.
precise: HIP's __ballot returns unsigned long long; on wave64 all 64 bits are used, so storing it in 32 bits loses lanes 32 to 63.
source: HIP 5.7 headers (H1 of F7-20)

simple: the chosen block and tile sizes for each GPU, kept in one place.
analogy: a small sheet per hall saying how big the trays and rows should be.
precise: per-device parameters chosen at run time from device properties (or per device pass for device-only constants), each with the measurement that justifies it.
source: C1 of F7-20 (map only, AH-4)

simple: parts of a wave that have nothing to do.
analogy: helpers in a row standing still.
precise: lanes whose execution-mask bit is off; a 32-work-item workgroup on a wave64 target is one wave with at most 32 active lanes (50 %).
source: half_isa run of F7-20
